questions.prompt: Which SI unit would you use to record the temperature of a science experiment?
questions.explanation: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of temperature; metre is for length, kilogram for mass and second for time.

questions.prompt: The tiny central part of an atom that holds the protons and neutrons is called the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the dense centre of the atom containing protons and neutrons; electrons move around it.

questions.prompt: Which of these substances has a sour taste and turns blue litmus red?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is an acid; acids taste sour and turn blue litmus paper red, while the others are bases.

questions.prompt: Which body system gives the body its shape and protects soft organs like the brain?
questions.explanation: The skeletal system (bones) supports the body, gives it shape and protects organs such as the brain and heart.

questions.prompt: The natural place where a particular animal or plant lives is called its:
questions.explanation: A habitat is the natural home where a living thing finds the food, water and shelter it needs.

questions.prompt: What is the Sun classified as?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star at the centre of the solar system; planets and moons orbit around it.

questions.prompt: Which part of a simple electric circuit supplies the energy to make the current flow?
questions.explanation: The cell or battery is the source of electrical energy that pushes the current around the circuit.

questions.prompt: Anything that has mass and takes up space is called:
questions.explanation: Matter is defined as anything that has mass and occupies space; everything around us is made of matter.

questions.prompt: Convert 4 kilometres into metres.
A rectangular field is 8 m long and 3 m wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a rectangle = length × width = 8 m × 3 m = 24 m², measured in square metres.

questions.prompt: An atom of aluminium has atomic number 13 and mass number 27. How many protons does it have?
questions.explanation: The atomic number equals the number of protons, so aluminium has 13 protons.

questions.prompt: How many atoms are in one molecule of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄?
questions.explanation: 2 hydrogen + 1 sulfur + 4 oxygen = 7 atoms in total.

questions.prompt: A cleaning liquid has a pH of 12. Which statement about it is correct?
options: It is the same as pure water
questions.explanation: A pH well above 7 means the substance is strongly basic (alkaline); pH 7 would be neutral.

questions.prompt: A student is given four compounds: sugar, table salt, methane and water. Which set contains only organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Organic compounds contain carbon bonded to hydrogen; only sugar and methane (CH₄) fit, while table salt and water are inorganic.

questions.prompt: In which organ does the churning action and acid begin to digest proteins?
questions.explanation: The stomach churns food and uses acid and enzymes to begin breaking down proteins.

questions.prompt: Which type of digestion is taking place when saliva breaks down starch in the mouth?
questions.explanation: Saliva contains an enzyme that chemically breaks down starch, so this is chemical digestion.

questions.prompt: In the food chain algae → small fish → big fish → kingfisher, which organism is the producer?
questions.explanation: Algae are plant-like organisms that make their own food using sunlight, so they are the producer that starts the chain.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a non-renewable resource?
options: A resource that is quickly replaced by nature
A resource that runs out and cannot be replaced in a short time
A resource that grows back every year
A resource that never gets used up
questions.explanation: Non-renewable resources, such as coal and minerals, form very slowly and run out once used.

questions.prompt: Which group of planets is small, rocky and located closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: The inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are small, rocky and nearest the Sun, while the outer planets are large gas giants.

questions.prompt: On a sunny day, the metal body of a car becomes hot even though nothing touches it. The heat reaches it mainly by:
questions.explanation: Heat from the Sun travels through empty space and air as radiation, warming the car without direct contact.

questions.prompt: Why can you NOT hear any sound coming directly through the empty space between the Sun and Earth?
options: There is no medium (air) in space for sound to travel through
questions.explanation: Sound needs a material medium such as air to travel; space is a vacuum, so sound cannot pass through it.

questions.prompt: A liquid has a mass of 250 g and a volume of 500 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume = 250 g ÷ 500 cm³ = 0.5 g/cm³.

questions.prompt: A runner covers 100 metres in 20 seconds. What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 100 m ÷ 20 s = 5 m/s.

questions.prompt: A neutral atom has a mass number of 31 and contains 16 neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explanation: Protons = mass number − neutrons = 31 − 16 = 15. A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons, so it has 15 electrons.

questions.prompt: How many atoms are present in three molecules of water, H₂O?
questions.explanation: One H₂O molecule has 2 + 1 = 3 atoms, so three molecules have 3 × 3 = 9 atoms.

questions.prompt: A student adds a base drop by drop to an acid until the mixture reaches pH 7. What has happened to the acid and base?
options: They have neutralized each other to form a salt and water
They have turned into a gas
questions.explanation: Adding a base to an acid until pH 7 is a neutralization reaction, producing a salt and water with no acid or base left over.

questions.prompt: Why is it an advantage that the small intestine is very long and folded?
options: It gives a large surface area to absorb digested food efficiently
questions.explanation: A long, folded small intestine has a very large inner surface, allowing more digested food to be absorbed into the blood.

questions.prompt: In a grassland, the number of grasshoppers suddenly increases greatly. What is the most likely immediate effect on the grass they feed on?
options: The amount of grass decreases as more is eaten
The grass turns into a consumer
questions.explanation: More grasshoppers eat more grass, so the grass (their food source) is used up faster and decreases.

questions.prompt: Overgrazing by too many cattle on a hillside often leads to soil erosion because:
options: The cattle add nutrients to the soil
Plant roots that hold the soil together are removed, so rain washes the soil away
The soil becomes too wet to move
questions.explanation: Grazing removes the plant cover and roots that bind the soil, so rain and wind can carry the loose soil away.

questions.prompt: Saturn is the 6th planet from the Sun. Which planet lies immediately between Saturn and the Sun?
questions.explanation: The order from the Sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn; so Jupiter lies just before Saturn.

questions.prompt: Two bulbs are connected side by side (in parallel) to one cell. If one bulb is removed, what happens to the other bulb?
options: It goes off because the circuit is broken
It keeps glowing because it still has its own complete path
questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit each bulb has its own separate path to the cell, so removing one bulb does not break the path of the other.

questions.prompt: A student wants to keep a cup of hot tea warm for as long as possible. Which choice of cup material and explanation is best?
options: A metal cup, because metal is a good insulator
A plastic or clay cup, because these are poor conductors and slow heat loss
A thin metal cup, because it lets heat escape quickly
Any cup, because the material makes no difference
questions.explanation: Plastic and clay are insulators (poor conductors), so they slow the transfer of heat out of the tea, keeping it warm longer than a metal cup would.

questions.prompt: A student investigates whether warmer water dissolves sugar faster. Which is the dependent variable (the factor measured) in this experiment?
options: The time taken for the sugar to dissolve
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is what you measure as a result; here the student measures the time taken for the sugar to dissolve at each temperature.

questions.prompt: Two atoms have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. Which statement best describes them?
options: They are the same element but have different mass numbers
questions.explanation: The number of protons (atomic number) fixes the element, so they are the same element; differing neutron numbers give them different mass numbers.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains how the digestive and circulatory systems work together?
options: The circulatory system chews the food
The digestive system breaks food into small molecules, which the circulatory system then carries to body cells
The digestive system pumps blood while the circulatory system makes enzymes
They do not interact at all
questions.explanation: The digestive system breaks food into small molecules and absorbs them into the blood, and the circulatory system then transports those nutrients to cells throughout the body.

questions.prompt: A planet is found that is very close to its star, small, and made of rock with almost no atmosphere. Based on what you know about our solar system, this planet is most like:
questions.explanation: Small, rocky planets close to the star with thin atmospheres resemble the inner planets such as Mercury and Mars, not the large gas giants.
